On appeal, Cummings argues that her original action was filed within the statute of limitations because the two-year statute of limitations would have expired on a Saturday, and under OCGA § 1-3-1 (d) (3), she had until the following Monday to file her lawsuit. We agree. OCGA § 9-3-33 provides that actions for personal injury must be brought within two years after the right of action accrues. Under OCGA § 1-3-1 (d) (3), when a period of time prescribed for “the exercise of any privilege” is measured in years, “the first day shall not be counted but the last day shall be counted; and, if the last day falls on 2 Saturday or Sunday, the party having such privilege . . . shall have through the following Monday to exercise the privilege[.]” OCGA § 1-3-1 (d) (3) applies to personal injury actions governed by the two-year statute of limitation in OCGA § 9-3- 33. Infinite Energy, Inc. v. Pardue, 310 Ga. App. 355, 362 (4) (713 SE2d 456) (2011); see generally Gardner v. Hyster Co., 785 FSupp. 161, 162-163 (MDGa. 1992) (discussing this Court’s history of applying amended OCGA § 1-3-1 (d) (3) to OCGA § 9-3-33); Mohar v. Leguizamo, 373 Ga. App. 230, 235-236 (1) (b) n.19 (907 SE2d 923) (2024) (where the two-year statute of limitation began running on February 8, 2018, it expired on February 10, 2020, since February 8, 2020, fell on a Saturday). Here, Cummings was injured on August 12, 2021, and because August 12, 2023, fell on a Saturday, her complaint was timely filed on Monday, August 14, 2023. Gullatt v. Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, 248 Ga. propositions.claim: For a Georgia personal-injury action, the supplied 2025 Court of Appeals excerpt states that the claim must be brought within two years after the right of action accrues. It also holds that when the two-year deadline falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the statutory weekend rule extends the filing deadline through the following Monday. This is general information; the excerpt does not address other claim-specific rules or exceptions.
propositions.quote: actions for personal injury must be brought within two years after the right of action accrues

propositions.claim: The same opinion applies that weekend extension to the case before it: the injury occurred August 12, 2021, the two-year anniversary fell on Saturday, August 12, 2023, and a complaint filed Monday, August 14, 2023, was timely.
